items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: a clarinet player that worked with him for a while was Peanuts Hucko, a wonderful clarinetist.

ctx.x: What about working with, you know I hear an awful lot of stories about Eddie Condon.

I played with him occasionally, you know, I wasn’t the number one clarinet player with him, I’ll be very honest with you. The number one clarinetist was Pee Wee Russell. And then when Pee Wee Russell wasn’t able to make it they used Tony Parenti, a wonderful Dixieland clarinetist from New Orleans. And then they used other musicians, a clarinet player that worked with him for a while was Peanuts Hucko, a wonderful clarinetist. But when they couldn’t get these clarinetists that I mentioned then they came to me. I…
So you’d get a gig — when you went to a club to get a gig, did you have an actual band in mind or did you get the gig and then find the musicians to do it?
